head.h1: Mediterranean Catering in Dubai — Prices, Formats and What You Get

opening_paragraph: Mediterranean catering in Dubai starts from AED 700 per person — grilled fish, seafood and mezze served the way the coast eats: bright, olive-oil-led and made for grazing. The style suits the climate and the way people entertain here, from a poolside lunch to a plated villa dinner. MyCHEF matches you with a vetted chef who designs the menu, cooks on site, serves and clears away, so the food does the talking and you stay a guest at your own table. Send the date, guest count and venue and you will have a full itemised quote promptly during our published business hours.

new_paragraphs: Our chefs cater the whole city, so wherever you are hosting there is a Mediterranean catering company in Dubai within reach. We regularly cook in Palm Jumeirah and Emirates Hills villas, Dubai Marina and JBR apartments, Downtown and Business Bay penthouses, and garden homes in Jumeirah, Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills. Beach clubs, rooftops and yachts are all part of the mix, and the mobile-kitchen setup means the same menu travels without losing quality. Pair the cuisine with a healthy or pescatarian brief, or browse all cuisines and sample menus . Planning a larger occasion? Start at catering in Dubai and we will pull the whole event together.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What Mediterranean catering in Dubai includes
new_paragraphs: It is a complete service, not a food drop unless you want one. A menu is designed around your event, a chef cooks it fresh in front of your guests, and a small front-of-house team handles service, plating, setup and cleanup. The Mediterranean food catering itself spans the whole basin — Greek and Levantine mezze, grilled sea bass and prawns, slow-roasted lamb, tabbouleh and fattoush, hummus, labneh and warm flatbread, olive-oil-dressed grains and roasted vegetables, finished with baklava or fresh fruit. Everything is prepared halal by default. Formats range from a shared mezze table to plated three-course dinners and live grill stations. Because this is a genuine mediterranean catering service, not a fixed package, portions, courses and staffing all flex to the room — an intimate dinner for eight or a standing reception for two hundred.

add_block.new_heading: Greek catering, Lebanese catering, or the whole basin
new_paragraphs: The Mediterranean is a long coastline and most enquiries arrive wanting one end of it. Greek catering in Dubai is the Aegean end — the tzatziki, melitzanosalata and taramosalata board, souvlaki and paidakia off the charcoal, whole sea bass with horta, moussaka, and loukoumades fried to order. Lebanese catering in Dubai is the Levantine end of the same table: hummus, moutabel, muhammara and labneh, tabbouleh and fattoush, warak enab, kibbeh, sambousek and fatayer, shish tawook and kofta from the grill, samak harra, then baklava and kunafa. Both are drawn from the menu below, so you can run one on its own or put them side by side — a five-dip Greek board next to a Levantine mezze spread reads as one long table, not two cuisines arguing. Tell the chef which end you lean towards and the balance is set from there.

And yes, Dubai has Mediterranean food in real depth. Levantine cooking has been part of ordinary eating in this city for decades, with Greek, Turkish, Italian and North African kitchens following it in, so the cuisine is native to the local market, not an import. For catering that matters in three practical ways: the ingredients are available year-round, chefs who cook this food for a living are not hard to match to your event, and a Mediterranean menu will not read as unfamiliar to any guest list in Dubai.

add_block.new_heading: The Mediterranean catering menu, course by course
new_paragraphs: This is the full working menu, written the way the cuisine is eaten. The table fills with dips and mezze first, the sea arrives next, then the charcoal grill, then one slow-cooked dish that has been in the oven since morning. Nothing here is a placeholder. Pick a section, pick the dishes, and the chef builds the run sheet around them. A mediterranean catering dubai menu is assembled from these lines, not chosen off a laminated card. If you came looking for mediterranean catering menu ideas, this is the raw material.
Dips and spreads, where every Greek table starts
Five distinct dips, offered on their own or as a sharing board. This section tells you whether a kitchen knows the cuisine.
Tzatziki : strained yoghurt, cucumber, garlic and fresh herbs.
Melitzanosalata : slow-roasted eggplant purée with peppers and herbs.
Fava : Santorini split peas with lemon juice, capers, spring onion, semi-dried tomato and olive oil.
Tirokafteri : feta whipped with fresh red chilli, paprika and pine nuts.
Taramosalata : cod roe, lemon zest, cold-pressed olive oil.
The Greek meze platter (three dips) or the five dip board , with charcoal-grilled pita in traditional, volcano or whole wheat.
Levantine crossover for a mixed room: hummus , moutabel , muhammara , labneh with olives .
Cold mezze and grazing boards
Boards come at 12-inch and 16-inch, and scale up into a fully styled grazing table from 25 guests.
Mediterranean meze board, classic meze board, veggie meze board, antipasto board, cheese and charcuterie board.
Warak enab : vine leaves stuffed with rice and herbs.
Kalamata olives with sundried tomato and mesclun.
Watermelon, feta and mint , and marinated feta with oregano and olive oil.
Fish marinato : yellowtail tartare with chives, red chilli, rosemary, garlic, oregano, lime and olive oil.
Hot mezze
Spanakopita : spinach, feta, fresh herbs, Greek yoghurt and thyme honey.
Cheese saganaki : fried kefalograviera from Epirus.
Fried kefalotyri saganaki : caramelised tomato jam, fresh fig, lemon and nuts.
Baked barrel-aged feta : roasted cherry tomato, olives and capers.
Keftedakia : Greek beef and lamb meatballs, pulses salad, Greek yoghurt.
Kolokythakia , crispy baby marrow, and tomato kefta with onion and mint.
Piperies ladoxido : padron peppers, garlic, vinegar and olive oil.
Hand-cut Greek fries , or oregano and feta fries with sea salt and paprika.
Falafel rocks , cheese sambousek , beef kibbeh , chevre and spinach in phyllo , spinach and cheese fatayer .
Homemade pie of the day , Cretan style.
From the sea
This section separates a real Mediterranean menu from a generic one, and the octopus is the tell. Slow-cooked first, then charred over coals.
Grilled octopus with fava, tomato paste and capers chutney.
Grilled octopus , chargrilled, with eggplant mousse, tomato, capers and salicornia.
Prawns saganaki : queen prawns, tomato sauce, red capsicum, feta and sourdough, made without the ouzo finish.
Fried calamari with black garlic mayo, or grilled calamari with horta, tomato, onion, lemon and olive oil.
Crispy whitebait with citrus mayo and lemon, and harissa-spiced prawn .
Salads
Horiatiki , the village salad: feta, tomato, cucumber, green bell pepper, onion, Kalamata olives, oregano, olive oil.
Santorini : sweet cherry tomatoes, capers, roasted bell pepper, spring onion, pita with graviera, sweet wine vinaigrette.
Cretan salad : cherry tomatoes, Greek feta, barley rusk, oregano and olive oil.
Heirloom beetroot salad : roasted baby beetroot, yoghurt and feta mousse, walnuts, apple, popped quinoa.
Lentil and manouri salad : green lentil, baby spinach, chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, caramelised pumpkin seeds, grilled manouri.
Watermelon and halloumi salad , revythosalata with bell pepper confit and feta, fattoush and tabbouleh .
From the charcoal grill
Paidakia : lamb chops marinated in fresh herbs, grilled over open fire and sliced.
Chicken souvlaki with pita, tzatziki and Greek fries.
Bifteki : beef and lamb patty, yoghurt and feta sauce, sautéed potatoes, kefalograviera.
Kontosouvli beef : slow-roasted beef loin off the chargrill.
Filetto : grilled beef fillet, crushed Kalamata olives, barrel-aged feta, tomato, florina pepper coulis.
Ribeye on the bone in olive oil, garlic and thyme, flame grilled, or striploin with beef pastourma butter.
Roasted lemon oregano chicken : oregano and thyme marinated, slow roasted on the open-fire grill, garlic tahini sauce.
Beef kofta kebab and shish tawook .
Mixed grill for sharing : chicken souvlaki, lamb chops, biftekia, striploin, halloumi, Greek fries, vegetables and tzatziki.
Whole fish and seafood mains
Catch of the day : whole sea bass or black bream, grilled with lemon oil and served with horta.
Grilled whole calamari : lemon olive oil, sweet tomato, kritamos, capers and spring onion.
Grilled tiger prawns : thyme and garlic marinated, chargrilled in the shell, on Greek salad with roasted red capsicum dip.
Grilled octopus and bean salad : paprika, lemon oil, Santorini fava bean salad and salicornia.
Fish fillet and seafood orzo : kritharaki pasta, fresh tomatoes, calamari and baby prawns.
Samak harra , Moroccan spiced grilled fish and seafood paella .
Kouzina, the oven and slow-cooked mains
Moussaka : potatoes, eggplant, minced meat and béchamel.
Vegetarian moussaka : layered potatoes, eggplant and zucchini in tomato sauce with béchamel and cheese. It sits on the menu beside the original, not in place of it.
Kleftiko roast lamb : slow-cooked lamb shank with trahana, graviera, grilled green peppers and roasted potatoes.
Lamb pilafi : slow-cooked lamb, pilafi rice, wild oregano, lemon, olive oil and kefalograviera.
Gemista : peppers, zucchini and tomatoes stuffed with rice and herbs, with roasted potatoes.
Imam bayildi : aubergine, onion stew, feta, tomato, cinnamon and olive oil.
Pan-roasted chicken with eggplant and graviera purée, or spring chicken with potatoes, wild oregano and mustard.
Pastitsio and Moroccan lamb tagine .
Pitas and handhelds
Chicken pita : grilled chicken, tzatziki, tomato, onions and fries wrapped in grilled pita. Lamb pita is built the same way.
Chicken souvlaki wrap , souvlaki skewers with grilled pita and fries, and gyros .
Moussaka burger : beef patty, caramelised onions, grilled eggplant, potato and cheesy béchamel.
Canapés and mini bites

For a standing reception the same food is rebuilt small: one filling on one base, so it can be eaten in a single bite with a drink in the other hand. Bases are tartlet, crostini, blini, skewer or a hollowed cucumber shell. Sold in tiers of six, eight or ten pieces per guest.
Tzatziki, melitzanosalata or tirokafteri piped onto crostini or into cucumber shells.
Watermelon, feta and mint on a skewer, and marinated feta with oregano.
Keftedakia on a skewer with Greek yoghurt, and spanakopita cut to bite size.
Chicken souvlaki off the skewer, tzatziki on top.
Fish marinato or crispy whitebait on a blini with citrus mayo.
Loukoumades served warm from the station as a sweet bite.
Sides
Greek oven-baked potatoes, oregano and feta fries, Greek rice pilaf, burgol pilaf.
Horta, the steamed wild greens, plus couscous salad and Mediterranean grilled vegetables.
Cauliflower with almonds and sea salt, asparagus with hazelnuts.
Dessert
Loukoumades : doughnuts with honey, chocolate sauce and walnuts.
Baklava cheesecake : baked cheesecake layered with mixed nuts in phyllo, cinnamon and syrup.
Orange pie : phyllo pastry, orange syrup, caramelised pumpkin seeds, orange cream and vanilla ice cream.
Greek coffee tiramisu : almond biscuit infused with Greek coffee and mascarpone.
Sweet taste of Greece , a selection of desserts for two.
Baklava , kunafa , galaktoboureko-style phyllo custard, ice cream platter, fresh fruit platter.
Greek-tails and drinks, all alcohol-free

Signature Greek-tails named after where they come from: Chios , Crete with lemon, rosemary honey and mastiha, Syros with loukoumia, rose water, pistachio, grapefruit and rose petals, and Patra with watermelon and mint.
Home-made mint lemonade, strawberry lemonade, virgin mojito in strawberry or passion fruit.
Greek coffee, mint tea, jellab, rose sharbat.
Live stations, if you want the cooking in the room

Live stations are where this cuisine earns its reputation, and they lean on equipment more than on the menu. Each one below is offered subject to the assigned culinary partner confirming the equipment, and the venue confirming fire and extraction clearance. We check that before it goes into your proposal, not after.
Charcoal and open-fire grill : paidakia, souvlaki and whole fish cooked in front of guests.
Gyro and kontosouvli spit , carved to order onto warm pita.
Build-your-own pita : grilled meats, the five dips, salads and fries laid out to assemble.
Flambéed saganaki : kefalograviera fired at the pass.
Loukoumades station , fried and honeyed to order. It is the piece of theatre guests talk about longest.
Diets, allergens and how the menu is marked

Every dish is coded on the printed menu, item by item, instead of carrying one footnote at the bottom: V vegetarian, VG vegan, D dairy, N nuts, S seafood, SS sesame. Dairy matters more in this cuisine than in most. Feta, graviera, kefalograviera, manouri, halloumi and yoghurt run through nearly every section, and nuts turn up in tirokafteri, the beetroot salad and most of the desserts. Menus are halal by default and pork is not served. The vegan line is genuinely deep here: fava, melitzanosalata, kolokythakia, piperies ladoxido, tomato kefta, hand-cut Greek fries, gemista, horta and the cauliflower and asparagus sides all belong to it.

Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event.
Minimums, portions and how far ahead to book
Minimum headcount : 10 guests for volume formats such as drop-off, platters and working lunch, and 20 guests for a buffet. A private chef cooking plated at your table has no minimum headcount.
Minimum order value : AED 900.
Portioning : salads and hot mezze are built in batches, so selections are taken by the item, not by the plate. Grazing tables start at 25 guests.

Lead time guidance : around 72 hours for a standard catering package, 3 to 5 days once live stations or multi-staff service are involved, 5 to 7 days for a bespoke menu, and 7 to 14 days for a wedding or a large corporate function.

We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. Tight timeline for your mediterranean? We check live partner availability before saying yes or no.

add_block.new_heading: Fresh, healthy and dietary-friendly by design
new_paragraphs: Mediterranean cooking is one of the few cuisines that is genuinely light and indulgent at once, which is a real advantage in Dubai's climate. Olive oil, grilled instead of fried proteins, generous vegetables and whole grains mean guests eat well without feeling weighed down at a summer or poolside event. That makes it a natural pick for health-conscious tables, beach and garden dining, and daytime celebrations where heavy food would flag. It also flexes to real dietary needs: allergen-aware preparation, labelled dishes and separate handling where it matters. Everything is halal, and the same menu can quietly serve keto, low-carb and pescatarian guests alongside the rest of the table — no separate sad plate. Good hosting is invisible, and a menu this adaptable lets one table suit a whole guest list.

If what you want is daily Mediterranean meals instead of a one-off event — the same grilled fish, grain salads and vegetable-led plates cooked ahead and portioned for the week — that is weekly meal prep , not catering. It is a different product priced by the week, and it is the right one if the goal is how you eat on a Tuesday, not how you host on a Saturday.

new_paragraphs: How much does Mediterranean catering cost in Dubai?

From around AED 700 per person, quoted to your guest count, menu and service. Buffet and drop-off formats cost less per head than plated service with staff, and packages can fix a per-person rate for a predictable budget.
What's included in the service?
A vetted chef, service staff where needed, plating, setup and cleanup are all handled for you. Menu design and, for larger events, a tasting are part of it too — one team runs the event end to end.
How do I hire a Mediterranean caterer in Dubai?
Share your date, guest count and venue; we match a vetted chef and send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day. A tasting is arranged for plated and larger events.
Can the menu be vegetarian, vegan or gluten-free?
Yes. Mediterranean cooking is naturally plant-forward, so full vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free and pescatarian menus are all catered for, and everything is prepared halal by default.
Do you offer a private Mediterranean chef at home?

Yes. A private Mediterranean chef can cook in your own kitchen for a dinner at home, or bring equipment and live stations for larger gatherings — Mediterranean home catering is one of our most-booked formats.
Is Mediterranean catering good for large corporate events?
Yes. Mezze spreads, grilled-fish stations and grazing tables scale cleanly from an intimate dinner to a corporate gala for hundreds, and the lighter food suits Dubai's climate.
How far in advance should I book?

About 72 hours suits a standard catering package, 3 to 5 days once live stations are involved, and 7 to 14 days for a wedding or large corporate function. Short-notice requests are still assessed individually — just ask.
Does Dubai have Mediterranean food?

Yes, and more of it than almost any cuisine in the city apart from Indian. Levantine cooking has been everyday food in Dubai for decades, with Greek, Turkish, Italian and North African kitchens alongside it, so the ingredients and the chefs are both here year-round.
Can you do a Lebanese or a Greek menu specifically?

Yes. MyCHEF's Mediterranean menu holds both: a Greek run of dips, souvlaki, whole fish and loukoumades, or a Lebanese run of hummus, moutabel, tabbouleh, kibbeh, shish tawook, samak harra and kunafa. You can also mix the two on one table.
What is the leading catering company in Dubai?

No single company leads catering in Dubai — the market splits between hotel catering arms, high-volume buffet operators and chef-led services like myCHEF, and the best fit depends on whether you are buying volume, a venue, or a chef cooking in front of your guests. Judge on published prices, a named chef, an itemised quote and who is accountable on the night; our guide to choosing a catering company in Dubai sets out the checks.
For mediterranean catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .
